summary: This is a reference page for the AS_TIME function, which casts a VARIANT value to a time value and does not convert from timestamps. It gives the syntax AS_TIME( variant_expr ), which takes a single VARIANT expression as its argument. An example creates a table multiple_types with VARIANT columns, inserts a TO_TIME('12:34:56') value wrapped in TO_VARIANT, and selects AS_TIME(time1), returning 12:34:56.
one_line: Reference for the AS_TIME function, which casts a VARIANT value to a time value, with a worked example.
key_facts: AS_TIME casts a VARIANT value to a time value.
AS_TIME does not convert from timestamps.
The syntax of AS_TIME is AS_TIME( <variant_expr> ).
The argument variant_expr is an expression that evaluates to a value of type VARIANT.
The example creates a table named multiple_types with columns binary1, date1, decimal1, time1, and timestamp1, all of type VARIANT.
The example inserts TO_VARIANT(TO_BINARY('F0A5')) into binary1.
The example inserts TO_VARIANT(TO_DATE('2018-10-10')) into date1.
The example inserts TO_VARIANT(TO_DECIMAL(1.23, 6, 3)) into decimal1.
The example inserts TO_VARIANT(TO_TIME('12:34:56')) into time1.
The example inserts TO_VARIANT(TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ('2018-10-10 12:34:56')) into timestamp1.
The query SELECT AS_TIME(time1) AS "Time" FROM multiple_types returns the value 12:34:56.
The function is listed under the Cast category and the semistructured data function group.
